distractors.reason: 'Highly certain' is grammatical but formal. 'Dead certain' is the informal intensifier.
'Deeply certain' is not idiomatic. 'Deeply' suits emotion or depth.
'Greatly certain' is not used. 'Greatly' describes amount of change or feeling.

example_sentence: She was ___ certain the plan would work.
l1_interference: يميل المتحدثون بالعربية إلى استخدام 'very' أو 'highly' في الكلام العادي، بينما 'dead' هي الكلمة الطبيعية في الإنجليزية غير الرسمية.
common_mistake: very certain (in informal speech it sounds stiff)
explanation: 'Dead certain' is an informal intensifier meaning completely certain. It is common in spoken English.

related_collocations.example: He was dead serious about the deadline.
After the trip I was dead tired.
The team was deeply convinced of the result.

memory_tip: DEAD + adjective = completely (informal) | HIGHLY = formal degree
